changedEndpoints.title: Choose the implementation substrate and public package coordinates
changedEndpoints.body:
## Question

Which implementation language and toolchain, package and command coordinates, source layout, minimum platform versions, dependency-lock rules, and reviewed-source bootstrap constraints should define the first release-ops core distribution?

The answer must preserve the settled provider-neutral contract and public/private ownership boundary. It must not choose command grammar, wire shapes, or adapter transports beyond what the implementation substrate forces.

comments.body:
I've settled the first distribution as one native Rust package containing Codiquarium's reusable library and the thin `cophax` executable. This records the accepted substrate choices and applies the [retained naming decision](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/blob/b1656b63bd7d271321bff9258fa6bcce34c0d01c/docs/research/CRYPTO_RELEASE_OPS_NAMING.md).

| Surface | Coordinate |
| --- | --- |
| Project and repository | Codiquarium; `nisavid/codiquarium`, by renaming the existing repository |
| Public operator | Codophylax |
| Cargo package and library crate | `codiquarium` |
| Executable | `cophax` |

The repository rename and source-facing naming migration precede implementation. They preserve repository identity, issue history, existing policy, and release protections. No package is published or reserved by this decision.

The source shape is one root Cargo package, not a workspace. `src/lib.rs` owns reusable logic; `src/main.rs` handles presentation and orchestration. Keep deterministic policy, parsing, validation, and state-transition logic self-contained, with cryptographic implementations and provider effects behind narrow adapters. Executable adapter modules belong in `src/adapters/`; the established top-level `adapters/` directory remains the public adapter-contract and conformance surface. Preserve the other existing top-level domains. A second crate or workspace requires a demonstrated dependency, privilege, platform, or release-cadence seam.

Use Rust edition 2024, pin Rust 1.98.1 exactly in `rust-toolchain.toml`, and set `rust-version = "1.98.1"` in `Cargo.toml`. Authoritative builds use that exact stable toolchain. Newer compilers may be experimental but produce no accepted artifact; nightly and unstable features are excluded. Before 1.0, a compiler change is a reviewed closure update, not an automatic compatibility promise. Go remains a deliberate fallback only if the dependency or implementation shape defeats end-to-end auditability; it is not a second implementation or an automatic fallback.

Commit `Cargo.lock`, the complete versioned `vendor/` tree for the selected dependencies, and `.cargo/config.toml`. Authoritative Cargo builds use `--frozen`. Builds have no network access, opaque downloads, or unpinned generation. Git dependencies, build scripts, procedural macros, unsafe dependencies, and native linkage are default-denied; each exception requires qualification and renewed review. An admitted build script must run from vendored, locked source. Native FFI is admitted only when a required reviewed implementation forces that seam and receives separate cross-platform qualification.

Bind the compiler, Cargo, standard-library artifacts, linker, Linux build image, and macOS SDK/Xcode inputs by exact version and digest where distributable. These are explicit trusted build inputs: genesis does not recursively audit or bootstrap Rust, LLVM, libc, or the Apple SDK. Independently rebuild the same frozen closure on another host and compare the resulting evidence. Acceptance binds reviewed source, dependencies, toolchain, build inputs and process, independent rebuild, and resulting artifact digests. Byte reproducibility is a per-target qualification property where supported, not a demand for identical bytes across different target platforms.

The initial acceptance targets are:

- `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`: Linux kernel 6.8 or later and glibc 2.39 or later;
- `aarch64-apple-darwin`: macOS 14 or later.

Other targets, including Linux arm64, macOS x86_64, and static musl, may receive inexpensive portability CI but have no pre-1.0 support claim until independently qualified.

This settles substrate and coordinates only. Command grammar, normative wire shapes, adapter transports, qualification, authority bootstrap, and production adoption stay with their owning tickets. The reviewed-source genesis and authenticated self-release gates remain intact. Existing `release-state/v1` and `admission-result/v1` identifiers remain unchanged; release writ and admission verdict are human-facing vocabulary.

<!-- resolution:2 -->

## Objective

Establish the accepted single-package Rust build surface for Codiquarium without implementing release or cryptographic behavior.

## Details

Use the settled substrate and coordinates: root Cargo package/library `codiquarium`, executable `cophax`, Rust edition 2024, exact Rust 1.98.1 toolchain and MSRV, `src/lib.rs`, thin `src/main.rs`, and the existing top-level contract/documentation domains. This is not a Cargo workspace.

Keep the library and binary non-operational placeholders. Add only the build metadata and checks needed to compile and test that skeleton. Apply the accepted lock/source configuration to actual dependencies; do not add dependencies merely to populate a vendor directory. This proves a build scaffold, not the qualified genesis closure or support for the minimum OS versions.

## Checklist

- [ ] The package, library, and binary names match the settled coordinates, with no workspace or second crate.
- [ ] Exact toolchain/MSRV and edition are declared. Commit `Cargo.lock` and `.cargo/config.toml`, plus the complete versioned `vendor/` tree for any actual dependencies.
- [ ] Build/test checks using `cargo --frozen` pass on both accepted target architectures, with actual runner/toolchain versions recorded.
- [ ] Existing repository-policy checks remain in force and pass on the reviewed commit.
- [ ] The scaffold provides no release, signing, verification, admission, installation, or provider operation and makes no genesis-qualification claim.

## Dependencies

Native dependency: Apply the Codiquarium repository identity before implementation.

## Notes

Use ordinary implementation and review models for the build-only work. Any newly required security decision goes to its owning decision ticket and permitted specialist route; it is not resolved by the scaffold. Tags, package publication, releases, real credentials, and host/provider changes remain outside this ticket.

Create `nisavid/cryptosacristy` as the public, independently versioned home of Cryptosacristy, the reusable cryptographic-operations product. Its public operator is Cryptosacrist and its prospective command is `sacrypt`.

## Scope

- Establish Apache-2.0 licensing, governance, DCO/contribution policy, security reporting, CI, release metadata, and the initial source and documentation layout.

- Create a repository-native Wayfinder map for implementation and first release.

Do not create keys, credentials, provider objects, host bindings, or releases in this ticket.

- The public repository exists with its required policy and CI surfaces.
- Its native implementation map names the genesis closure and first authenticated release.
- The dotfiles-to-public ownership handoff is explicit and reviewable.

AFK after repository-creation authority is confirmed.

comments.body:
The planned public repository is Cryptosacristy, with `nisavid/cryptosacristy` as its repository coordinate and `sacrypt` as the prospective command, per the [retained naming decision](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/blob/b1656b63bd7d271321bff9258fa6bcce34c0d01c/docs/research/CRYPTO_RELEASE_OPS_NAMING.md).

I'm applying the settled repository-only gate correction: [Define the repository domain model and disabled Sal extension boundary](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/143) does not block this value-free public scaffold. The established [reusable ownership boundary](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/207), [reference-adoption profile](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/217), and [operational delivery boundary](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/259) supply its repository-level scope.

The domain-model decision remains open and continues to block [Build and qualify the crypto-ops genesis closure](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/262) and its downstream adoption. Removing the provisioning edge neither resolves that decision nor authorizes keys, credentials, private bindings, provider resources, host changes, or production adoption. This issue remains open until the repository and its scoped acceptance evidence actually exist.
